# Task index (Museon CLI 1.2.0)

Museon CLI runs MuseOn's social-media operations from an Agent: UGC Campaigns (set up, recruit, approve, contract, daily tasks, content review, counting, client reports), content tracking Campaigns, analytics boards, social accounts and publishing, AI image posts, research and the organization. Find the task below, then run its commands in order. Every command prints one JSON envelope; reads change nothing; a write that reaches someone outside the organization or cannot be undone needs --yes, which only the user may give.

Run `museoncli guide <task-id>` for a task's steps with each command's required flags, risk and gotcha; `museoncli guide --search <words>` finds a task from the user's words.

## 0. Start here

Sign in, choose the organization, find a command, keep the CLI and its Skills current. Read the topics on ids and on the confirmation rule before your first write.

- **Sign in** (`login`): `museoncli auth start` → `museoncli auth finish` → `museoncli auth status` → `museoncli auth logout`
- **Choose the organization to act in** (`choose-organization`): `museoncli whoami` → `museoncli org list` → `museoncli org select` → `museoncli org current`
- **Find the command for a job** (`find-a-command`): `museoncli guide` → `museoncli schema`
- **Check the version, upgrade, install the Skills** (`keep-cli-current`): `museoncli version` → `museoncli upgrade` → `museoncli setup`

## 1. Run a UGC Campaign

A UGC Campaign in the order the work happens: create and set it up, recruit, approve applications, contract, run the day's tasks and messages, review content, decide what counts, report to the client and read settlement. Every `ugc` command takes the UGC Campaign id from `ugc campaign +list` as --campaign-id.

- **Find a UGC Campaign and its ids** (`ugc-find-campaign`): `museoncli ugc campaign +list` → `museoncli campaign-monitor agency-campaign +list` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +list` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +get` → `museoncli campaign-monitor campaign +get`
- **Create and set up a UGC Campaign** (`ugc-create-campaign`): `museoncli ugc campaign +create` → `museoncli ugc campaign-settings +update` → `museoncli ugc campaign-staff +set` → `museoncli ugc delivery-target +create` → `museoncli ugc contract-template +set` → `museoncli ugc payscale +create` → `museoncli ugc pay-rate +create` → `museoncli ugc discord-server +initialize` → `museoncli ugc brief +create` → `museoncli ugc campaign-setup +get` → `museoncli ugc campaign +launch`
- **Read how a Campaign is configured** (`ugc-read-setup`): `museoncli ugc campaign-setup +get` → `museoncli ugc campaign-settings +get` → `museoncli ugc campaign-staff +list` → `museoncli ugc delivery-target +list` → `museoncli ugc payscale +list` → `museoncli ugc contract-template +get` → `museoncli ugc discord-server +get` → `museoncli ugc dm-rule +list` → `museoncli ugc dm-automation +list`
- **Change a Campaign's settings, team, targets, payscales or Discord** (`ugc-change-setup`): `museoncli ugc campaign-settings +update` → `museoncli ugc campaign-staff +set` → `museoncli ugc delivery-target +update` → `museoncli ugc delivery-target +delete` → `museoncli ugc payscale +update` → `museoncli ugc payscale +delete` → `museoncli ugc pay-rate +update` → `museoncli ugc pay-rate +delete` → `museoncli ugc contract-template +set` → `museoncli ugc discord-server +set` → `museoncli ugc discord-server +remove`
- **Launch, pause, resume, end, archive or rename a Campaign** (`ugc-lifecycle`): `museoncli ugc campaign +launch` → `museoncli ugc campaign +pause` → `museoncli ugc campaign +resume` → `museoncli ugc campaign +complete` → `museoncli ugc campaign +archive` → `museoncli ugc campaign +restore` → `museoncli ugc campaign +rename`
- **Write and link Formats (脚本, brief)** (`ugc-formats`): `museoncli ugc brief-library +list` → `museoncli ugc brief-library +get` → `museoncli ugc brief-library +create` → `museoncli ugc brief-library +update` → `museoncli ugc brief-library +copy` → `museoncli ugc brief-library +archive` → `museoncli ugc brief +list` → `museoncli ugc brief +get` → `museoncli ugc brief +create` → `museoncli ugc brief +link` → `museoncli ugc brief +copy` → `museoncli ugc brief +update` → `museoncli ugc brief +upload-media` → `museoncli ugc brief +unlink`

- **Assign Formats to creators and link videos to Formats** (`ugc-assign-formats`): `museoncli ugc enrollment +list` → `museoncli ugc brief +progress` → `museoncli campaign-monitor assignment +list` → `museoncli ugc assignment +create` → `museoncli ugc assignment +update-terms` → `museoncli ugc assignment +withdraw` → `museoncli ugc creative +list` → `museoncli ugc creative +set-brief` → `museoncli ugc creative +apply-default-briefs`

## 2. Track content (content tracking Campaigns)

A content tracking Campaign follows creators' and posts' performance without applications or review. Create it, add what to track to its monitor collection, read the numbers. Everything after creation takes the collection id from `campaign-monitor +list` as --id.

- **Create a tracking Campaign and add creators or posts** (`tracking-create`): `museoncli ugc campaign +create` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +list` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +add-creators` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +add-content` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +list-creators` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +list-content`
- **Stop tracking creators or posts** (`tracking-remove`): `museoncli campaign-monitor +remove-creators` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +remove-content` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +bulk-remove-content`
- **Read a tracking Campaign's performance** (`tracking-performance`): `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-summary` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-period-performance` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +list-dimensions` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-breakdown` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +list-content` → `museoncli campaign-monitor creator-tag +list`
- **Read one account's or one post's synced history** (`account-and-post-history`): `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-creator` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +list-posts` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-creator-performance` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-post` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-post-performance` → `museoncli campaign-monitor +resolve-post`

## Topics

### Which id goes where

- `ugc ... --campaign-id` (and `ugc campaign +launch --id`) is the **UGC Campaign id** from `museoncli ugc campaign +list`. `analytics board --campaign-id` and `campaign-monitor agency-campaign +list` use the same Campaign ids.
- Every `campaign-monitor` command that reads one Campaign takes `--id` = the **monitor collection id** from `museoncli campaign-monitor +list`. It is a different id from the UGC Campaign id; never pass one for the other. `campaign-monitor campaign +get --id <collection>` tells you the UGC Campaign behind a collection.
- Inside a parent, `--id` is the entity the command acts on and the parent is qualified: `ugc enrollment +approve --campaign-id <campaign> --id <enrollment>`, `ugc assignment +withdraw --campaign-id <campaign> --id <assignment>`. In `campaign-monitor` the parent collection is `--id` and children are qualified (`--content-id`, `--collection-content-id`).
- An enrollment id (`ugc enrollment +list`) is one creator's place in one Campaign: approve, message, nudge, persona and payscale take it. A creative id is one video (`ugc creative +list`, `campaign-monitor video +list`); a content id is one post on one platform.
- A task id comes from `ugc task +list`; its `actions` list what `ugc task +run-action --action` accepts.
- Every id is a UUID; the CLI rejects placeholders before any request.

### The three creator ids

- **UGC creator** (a person, `ugc_creator_id`): `ugc creator +list`/`+get --id`; `campaign-monitor +list-content --ugc-creator-id`; `--creator-id` on `campaign-monitor video +list`, `settlement +get` and `enrollment +list`.
- **Social account** (one handle on one platform): `campaign-monitor +get-creator --id`, `+list-posts --creator-id`, `+get-creator-performance --id`, `+remove-creators --creator-id`, `+list-content --creator-id`. A social account's `creator_info.creator_id` is unrelated: never read the person from it or from a handle.
- **Enrollment** (the person in one Campaign): what every `ugc enrollment`/`message` write takes.
- The same flag name `--creator-id` means a person on some commands and a social account on others: read the flag's help (`<command> --help`) before passing it.

### The kinds of campaign

- **UGC Campaign** (`ugc`, `ugc campaign +create --type ugc`): creators apply, sign a contract, post against Formats (脚本, `brief` in commands) and are paid by payscales. Run by the operating team's organization.
- **Content tracking Campaign** (`ugc campaign +create --type tracking`): no applications or review; you add creators and posts to its monitor collection and read their performance (`campaign-monitor`).
- **Monitor collection** (`campaign-monitor +list`): the analytics side of either kind; every Dashboard read is keyed by it.
- **Agentic Creative Campaign** (`agentic-campaign`): MuseOn keeps publishing AI image posts on chosen accounts by persona Plans. Separate ids, its own lifecycle.
- HireAICreator plans and test groups (`hireaicreator`) are a separate product with their own Skill.

### Dry run, --yes and confirmation_required

- Every write takes `--dry-run`. On `ugc` and most newer commands the dry run reads the live state and shows what would change; elsewhere it validates and echoes the input. Nothing is written.
- A command that reaches someone outside the organization (messages, nudges, invitations, broadcasts, client reports, review verdicts) or cannot be undone needs `--yes`. Without it the CLI answers `ok: false, reason: confirmation_required` (exit 1) and, where it can, `preview`. Show the user the preview, ask, and only then rerun the same command with `--yes`. Never add `--yes` on your own.
- Plain writes (claim, comment, due date, persona, counting, settings) run without `--yes`; still dry-run first unless the user already decided exactly this change.
- `museoncli guide <task>` marks each step `read`, `write` or `destructive`, and `needs_yes`.

### Conflicts, retries and async work

- Compare-and-set: many writes send the version, status or `updated_at` they read (`--expected-version`, `--expected-status`, `--expected-updated-at`). A `conflict` means someone changed it since: read again, show the user, ask again. Never retry blindly.
- Idempotency: creates, messages and batch jobs return or take an `--idempotency-key`. After a timeout or unknown outcome, rerun with the same key and the same input; a new key does it twice.
- Async work returns a handle (task id, job id, batch id) and a matching `+get` command. A receipt is not completion: read the status until it is terminal, and use the returned wakeup delay instead of inventing one.
- A write is done only when its read-back says so (`+list`/`+get` of the same object).

### Organizations, roles and who may do what

- Every command acts in the selected organization (`museoncli org current`; change it with `museoncli org select --id <organization-id>`). `--organization-id <id>` addresses another organization for one call. Envelopes name it in `organization`.
- There is no workspace: no `workspace` command, no `--workspace-id`, except in `agentic-campaign` and `hireaicreator`.
- Your role in the organization (owner, admin, operator, member) and its Campaign scope decide what you see and change. UGC operations (approve, message, review, setup, client reports) belong to the Campaign's operating team: owner, admin, or an operator on that Campaign. A member reads.
- The server decides. A refusal is `not_found` or `forbidden`: tell the user this login cannot do it; never retry under another identity or organization.

### When a command fails

- Branch on `error.code` (same as `reason`), `error.server_code` and `error.retryable`; `error.hint` names the help to read on a usage error.
- `missing_auth` / `unauthorized`: run `museoncli auth start`, show the link, `museoncli auth finish --wait`, then resume. `missing_organization`: `museoncli org list`, `museoncli org select`.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failure, 2 usage, 3 not found, 4 authentication, 5 conflict.
- A read that lists pages: add `--all` and check `page_info.complete`, or follow `next_cursor` with `--cursor`.

### Which of two similar commands to use

| Need | Use | Not | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Find a UGC Campaign's id for ugc and analytics commands | `museoncli ugc campaign +list` | `museoncli campaign-monitor +list` | campaign-monitor +list returns monitor collection ids, which only campaign-monitor takes. |
| Find the id for Dashboard reads (campaign-monitor) | `museoncli campaign-monitor +list` | `museoncli ugc campaign +list` | Dashboard reads are keyed by the monitor collection. |
| A UGC Campaign's roster to act on (approve, assign, message, persona) | `museoncli ugc enrollment +list` | `museoncli campaign-monitor enrollment +list` | ugc returns the enrollment ids ugc writes take; campaign-monitor enrollment +list is the Operations tab view with contract and Discord state. |
| Creators of a UGC Campaign with their post figures | `museoncli campaign-monitor roster +list` | `museoncli ugc enrollment +list`, `museoncli campaign-monitor +list-creators` | roster +list is the By Creator tab; +list-creators lists tracked social accounts, the tracking Campaign view. |
| One creator (a person) and their Campaigns | `museoncli ugc creator +get` | `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-creator` | campaign-monitor +get-creator reads one social account by its social account id. |
| A UGC Campaign's videos and their review state | `museoncli campaign-monitor video +list` | `museoncli campaign-monitor +list-content`, `museoncli ugc creative +list` | video +list is the Content tab (each video once); +list-content lists every post with attribution and is the one for tracking Campaigns; ugc creative +list is the brief view for assigning Formats. |
| Approve or reject an application | `museoncli ugc enrollment +approve` | `museoncli ugc task +run-action` | Same effect. Working from the Tasks queue, press the task's own approve/reject with task +run-action; otherwise use enrollment +approve/+reject. |
| Approve or reject a video | `museoncli ugc creative +review` | `museoncli ugc task +run-action` | Same effect; from a review task use task +run-action --action approve\|reject. |
| Write to one creator | `museoncli ugc message +send` | `museoncli ugc broadcast +create`, `museoncli ugc enrollment +nudge` | A broadcast goes to many on Discord; a nudge is the fixed reminder for one check. |
| Daily trend and KPI tiles | `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-summary` | `museoncli campaign-monitor +get-period-performance` | +get-period-performance compares a period with the one before it. |
| Figures over several Campaigns | `museoncli analytics board +get-data` | `museoncli campaign-monitor agency-analytics +get` | A board reads the Campaigns it holds; agency-analytics +get is every UGC Campaign of the operating organization. |
| Publish ready video files or photo sets | `museoncli publish post +schedule` | `museoncli ai-slideshow publish +create-schedule`, `museoncli hireaicreator delivery +share` | ai-slideshow publish schedules slideshow accounts; hireaicreator delivery shares HireAICreator videos. |
| A UGC Format (脚本) | `museoncli ugc brief +list` | `museoncli ai-slideshow asset +list`, `museoncli hireaicreator format +list` | ai-slideshow asset --type format and hireaicreator format are different products' formats. |
| A UGC persona (creator type) | `museoncli ugc persona +list` | `museoncli ai-slideshow asset +list`, `museoncli hireaicreator persona +list` | ai-slideshow asset --type persona is a slideshow voice; hireaicreator persona an AI creator. |
| Generate one image or video from a prompt | `museoncli media +generate` | `museoncli ai-slideshow generation +create` | ai-slideshow generation +create builds an image post from format, topic and persona assets. |

### Renamed commands

Old command names keep answering, print a deprecation warning and will be removed. Use the new name.

`museoncli guide --search <old name>` names the command to use instead.

## Not in this index

- `hireaicreator.*`: HireAICreator (AI creators, video plans, test groups, warmup, delivery) has its own workflow; follow the museon-content-workflow-hireaicreator Skill and `museoncli schema hireaicreator`.
- `staff-ops.*`: MuseOn staff diagnostics (deployed code, logs, read-only tables); not for customer work.
